questions.question: Physical quantities can be classified based on magnitude and direction into which two groups?
questions.explanation: Physical quantities are grouped as scalars and vectors by magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Scalar quantities are fully described by which feature?
questions.explanation: Scalars require only magnitude for complete description.

questions.question: Which pair contains only scalar quantities?
questions.explanation: Mass and volume are both scalar quantities.

questions.question: Scalar quantities obey which rules?
questions.explanation: Scalars obey ordinary arithmetic rules.

questions.question: Adding 40 kg and 20 kg to get 60 kg illustrates which property?
questions.explanation: Scalar addition follows simple arithmetic.

questions.question: Which quantity is not scalar?
questions.explanation: Force is a vector quantity.

questions.question: Vector quantities require which pair?
questions.explanation: Vectors are described by both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Which list contains vector quantities only?
questions.explanation: Displacement and velocity are both vector quantities.

questions.question: The arrow symbol over a letter represents which type of quantity?
questions.explanation: An arrow or cap over a letter denotes a vector.

questions.question: A bold letter is used to represent which quantity?
questions.explanation: A bold letter is a common vector notation.

questions.question: In two dimensions a vector A is written as which expression?
questions.explanation: A two dimensional vector has x and y components along i and j.

questions.question: In three dimensions a vector A is expressed with how many unit vectors?
questions.explanation: Three dimensional vectors use i, j and k unit vectors.

questions.question: Two vectors are equal when they have which features?
questions.explanation: Equal vectors must have the same magnitude and direction.

questions.question: A unit vector has which magnitude?
questions.explanation: A unit vector has a magnitude of one.

questions.question: A null vector is characterized by which magnitude?
questions.explanation: A null vector has zero magnitude.

questions.question: A vector with magnitude one is called which type?
questions.explanation: A vector of magnitude one is a unit vector.

questions.question: A vector with zero magnitude is called which type?
questions.explanation: A zero magnitude vector is a null vector.

questions.question: Equality of vectors does not require which feature?
questions.explanation: Equal vectors need not act from the same position.

questions.question: Resolving a vector means finding which of the following?
questions.explanation: Resolution expresses a vector through its components.

questions.question: The unit vectors along x, y and z axes are represented by which symbols?
questions.explanation: Cartesian unit vectors are i, j and k.

questions.question: In two dimensions vector A equals Ax i plus Ay j. Ax and Ay are known as which term?
questions.explanation: Ax and Ay are the components of vector A.

questions.question: In three dimensions vector A equals Ax i plus Ay j plus Az k. The z-component is represented by which term?
questions.explanation: Az is the component along the z-axis.

questions.question: Unit vectors i, j and k point along which axes respectively?
questions.explanation: i, j and k correspond to x, y and z axes.

questions.question: The components of a vector can be expressed using which coordinate system?
questions.explanation: Cartesian coordinates express vectors through i, j and k components.

questions.question: A three dimensional vector has how many Cartesian components?
questions.explanation: A three dimensional vector has x, y and z components.

questions.question: The magnitude of a two dimensional vector is found using which theorem?
questions.explanation: Vector magnitude follows Pythagoras theorem.

questions.question: The length of an arrow representing a vector indicates which feature?
questions.explanation: Arrow length represents vector magnitude.

questions.question: The arrowhead on a vector diagram indicates which feature?
questions.explanation: The arrowhead shows the direction of the vector.

questions.question: Vector addition must consider which two features?
questions.explanation: Vector addition depends on both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Vector quantities do not obey which rules?
questions.explanation: Vectors do not obey ordinary arithmetic addition.

questions.question: The resultant of two or more vectors is obtained by which process?
questions.explanation: The resultant is found through vector addition.

questions.question: The magnitude of a vector in three dimensions can be found by extending which rule?
questions.explanation: Three dimensional magnitude extends Pythagoras theorem.

questions.question: Two vectors can be added graphically using which arrangement?
questions.explanation: Graphical vector addition uses the head to tail method.

questions.question: Multiplying a vector by a scalar produces which type of quantity?
questions.explanation: Scalar multiplication of a vector yields a vector.

questions.question: If vector A is multiplied by scalar m, the result is which expression?
questions.explanation: Scalar multiplication gives D equal to mA.

questions.question: Vector multiplication is done in how many main ways?
questions.explanation: Vectors are multiplied by scalars or by other vectors.

questions.question: The product of a vector and a scalar yields which type of quantity?
questions.explanation: A vector multiplied by a scalar remains a vector.

questions.question: The vector product is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: Vector product is also called cross product.

questions.question: The magnitude of A × B is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Cross product magnitude is |A||B| sin θ.

questions.question: The angle used in A × B is which angle between the vectors?
questions.explanation: The smaller angle between the vectors is used.

questions.question: The magnitude of A × B equals zero when the angle is which value?
questions.explanation: The sine of 0 degrees is zero.

questions.question: The vector product of two parallel vectors has which magnitude?
questions.explanation: Parallel vectors have zero cross product.

questions.question: The vector product of two perpendicular vectors has which sine value?
questions.explanation: The sine of 90 degrees is one.

questions.question: The direction of a cross product is perpendicular to which plane?
questions.explanation: Cross product direction is perpendicular to the plane of the vectors.

questions.question: In the vector product expression, which trigonometric function appears?
questions.explanation: The cross product uses the sine of the angle between vectors.

questions.question: The scalar product is also known by which name?
questions.explanation: Scalar product is also called dot product.

questions.question: The dot product of A and B is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Dot product magnitude is |A||B| cos θ.

questions.question: The dot product of two perpendicular vectors equals which value?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product.

questions.question: The dot product in component form is given by which expression?
questions.explanation: Component dot product sums products of matching components.

questions.question: The dot product of i and j equals which value?
questions.explanation: i and j are orthogonal unit vectors.
